AI-103 · Microsoft Learn study deck

AI-103 Flashcards

How this deck works

Every area of the exam, grouped by its domain and weight. Pick the best of four answers, or switch to flipping and saying the answer out loud. A wrong pick explains why it's wrong and what it belongs to. A right one moves to the next card after 1.5 seconds; click anywhere to stay and read. Every wrong answer goes into your review pile automatically, and + Add to review (or R) adds any card you want to see again; Review only drills that pile. Cards with a yellow edge and ★ test a skill named in the AI-103 study guide; use Study guide only to drill just those. Learn modules only keeps the cards whose topic is taught in the AI-103 Microsoft Learn modules and drops the ones that come only from other Microsoft docs. The counts on the chips follow whichever of these is on. Cards that name a function or setting have a Sample code tab on the answer side (or press S) showing it in real code from Microsoft's docs. Every card has a fixed number (#1 to #401) and every practice question a Q number (Q1 to Q118), in the top corner, so you can point to a specific one.

Concept cards are the ones to master. For Code cards, recognize the name and say what it does. Fill in the function shows real Microsoft sample code with one name blanked out: pick it from four choices (or switch to typing it), then press Enter for the next card.

How the real AI-103 works

  • 120 minutes. Most Microsoft exams have 40 to 60 questions; Microsoft doesn't publish AI-103's exact count.
  • The passing score is 700 on a scale of 1 to 1000. Scaled scores aren't a simple percentage, so treat this page's score as an estimate.
  • You can mark questions for review and use a review screen before you finish a section. Case studies come as their own section, and once you move past a section you can't go back to it. This mock works the same way.
  • You can open Microsoft Learn during the exam, but the timer keeps running and searching for every answer won't fit in the time.
  • Expect build-list, code-completion, Yes/No and multiple-response items, not just plain multiple choice.

Sources: AI-103 certification page · Exam duration and experience
